# Industrial-Services Unit: Turnaround-or-Exit Assessment & Decision Framework

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY: Diagnostic-Led Path to Profitability or Controlled Exit

**Primary Approach: Comprehensive 12-month diagnostic and decision framework that systematically diagnoses whether losses are structural (market position, competitive dynamics, fundamental profitability ceiling) or execution-driven (operational inefficiency, pricing power, go-to-market strategy failures), identifies profitable customer segments and service lines through rigorous margin analysis, designs a targeted turnaround plan with clear operational and financial milestones for Month 12 decision gate, and establishes parallel exit alternatives with triggering criteria—ensuring the board has both a credible path to sustainable profitability and a disciplined exit strategy if turnaround becomes unachievable.**

The diversified group should pursue a **three-stage decision framework (Diagnostic Phase Months 1-3, Turnaround Design Phase Months 4-6, Proof-of-Concept & Decision Phase Months 7-12)** combining rapid diagnostic work to distinguish structural losses from execution failures, granular segment and service-line profitability analysis to identify profit centers and loss drivers, targeted turnaround initiatives designed to recover $X-YM EBITDA by Month 12, and clear go/no-go decision criteria aligned to board expectations—with parallel exit planning ensuring management can move decisively to divestment if turnaround proves infeasible.

---

## PART 1: RAPID DIAGNOSTIC FRAMEWORK (MONTHS 1-3)

### 1.1 Financial & Operational Root-Cause Analysis

**Objective**: Determine whether losses are structural (unfixable without exiting market) or execution-driven (fixable through operational improvements, pricing, cost reduction, portfolio optimization).

#### Component 1A: Three-Year Loss Pattern Deep Dive

| Metric | Year -2 (Current -2) | Year -1 (Current -1) | Year 0 (Current) | Trend | Diagnostic Implication |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Revenue** | $500M (assumed baseline) | $510M (+2% growth) | $495M (-3% decline) | Declining growth → stagnation → decline | **Yellow flag**: Growth decelerated, now reversing. Indicates competitive pressure, customer loss, or market saturation. Not a pure revenue problem (still $500M+), but momentum negative. |
| **Gross Margin %** | 28% | 27% | 25% | -300 bps decline over 2 years | **RED FLAG - STRUCTURAL**: Each year, gross margin contracted 100-150 bps. Indicates: (a) price erosion in competitive bids; (b) cost inflation outpacing pricing; (c) unfavorable service-mix shift (high-margin services declining, low-margin growing). **Diagnosis needed**: Segment-level margin analysis to identify which customer segments/service lines are deteriorating. |
| **Gross Profit $** | $140M | $137.7M | $123.75M | -$16.25M (-12%) decline | **CRITICAL**: 12% decline in absolute gross dollars over 2 years. Cost structure cannot absorb (if fixed costs = 60-70% of gross margin historically). **Implication**: Even with cost-cutting, losses widened because gross-dollar decline exceeded cost reductions. |
| **SG&A as % of Revenue** | 22% ($110M) | 22% ($112.2M) | 23% ($113.85M) | Creeping up despite "restructuring" | **Execution problem**: Two restructuring rounds claiming cost-cutting, yet SG&A increased slightly. Suggests: (a) restructuring cuts offset by new hires/inflation; (b) ineffective cost discipline; (c) inefficient processes requiring higher overhead. |
| **EBITDA** | $18M (+3.6% margin) | -$2M (-0.4% margin) | -$10M (-2% margin) | Crossed from profitable to -$28M swing in 2 years | **CRITICAL DIAGNOSTIC**: Margin compression is severe. Unit was barely profitable, now deeply unprofitable. Restructuring failed to slow deterioration. |
| **EBIT / Operating Income** | $10M (+2% margin) | -$8M (-1.6% margin) | -$16M (-3.2% margin) | Worsening | Below EBITDA due to D&A ($8M assumed constant). |
| **Working Capital as % of Revenue** | 18% ($90M) | 19% ($96.9M) | 20% ($99M) | Increasing | **Cash drain**: Working capital increased $9M over 2 years despite lower revenue (inventory builds, DSO creeping, DPO issues). Indicates: (a) obsolete inventory; (b) customer payment delays; (c) poor inventory management. |
| **Order Book / Pipeline** | $1,200M (2.4x annual revenue) | $1,050M (2.06x annual revenue) | $850M (1.72x annual revenue) | -$200M decline; now at risk-floor | **CRITICAL**: Order book declining at 15-20% CAGR. At current burn rate, only 1.7x annual revenue remains (vs. historical 2.4x). If trend continues, revenue will fall to $400M by Year 2. Indicates: (a) loss of competitiveness in bidding; (b) customer churn; (c) declining market relevance. **Implication**: Turnaround must reverse order-book decline by Month 12 or unit becomes unviable. |
| **Customer Churn Rate** | ~5% annual (healthy) | ~8% annual | ~12% annual (estimated) | Accelerating customer loss | **CRITICAL**: Churn accelerated from 5% to 12% in 2 years. If top 10 customers = 40-50% of revenue, loss of 2-3 large customers = $20-50M revenue impact. **Diagnostic**: Which customers left? Were they lost to competition or internal service failures? |
| **Utilization Rate (Technicians/Field Staff)** | 75% | 70% | 65% | Declining despite headcount "cuts" | **Execution problem**: If utilization fell 10 points while revenue fell 3%, labor model is broken. Indicates: (a) overstaffing relative to billable work; (b) inefficient job scheduling; (c) project delays creating idle time. |
| **Pricing / Price Realization** | Industry +3% premium | Industry -1% discount | Industry -4% discount | Eroding competitive position | **STRUCTURAL RISK**: Unit pricing declined vs. market by 7 points in 2 years. Either: (a) unit losing contracts to lower-cost competitors; (b) customer concentration increasing (few large customers demanding discounts); (c) service quality declining, forcing price cuts. **Implication**: Fixing pricing requires either competitive advantage restoration or customer mix improvement. |

**Diagnostic Conclusion from 1A**:
- **Structural losses**: Gross margin compression (-300 bps) + price deterioration (-7 points vs. industry) + order-book decline (15-20% CAGR) suggest **fundamental competitive weakness**. Unit is losing bids, losing customers, and losing pricing power. These are **structural problems**, not just execution failure.
- **Execution failures** (compounding structural issues): Cost-cutting ineffective (SG&A still rising); working-capital management poor; utilization collapsing.
- **Verdict**: Mix of structural + execution problems. **Turnaround possible if**: (a) identify profitable customer segments to focus on (restore selective pricing power); (b) exit unprofitable segments/customers (stop negative-margin churn); (c) fix operational execution (utilization, cost structure, cash management). **Exit needed if**: (a) no profitable segment large enough to sustain fixed costs; (b) order-book decline cannot be reversed (structural market loss).

---

#### Component 1B: Customer Profitability Segmentation Analysis

**Objective**: Identify which customer segments/service lines are profitable (salvageable) and which are perpetually unprofitable (should be exited).

| Customer Segment | # Customers | Revenue | Gross Margin % | Gross Profit $ | EBITDA $ | EBITDA % | Margin Trend | Churn Rate | NPS / Satisfaction | Strategic Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Segment A: Tier-1 Strategic / Cross-Divisional** | 8-12 major | $200M (40% of revenue) | 32% | $64M | $24M | +12% | Stable (30-32% over 3 yrs) | 3% (low) | 45+ (strong) | **High**: Often buy from other divisions; provide cross-selling opportunities; sticky, long-term contracts. **Profitability**: Profitable, margin-accretive. **Issue**: Not growing; may be squeezed internally by other divisions demanding low prices. |
| **Segment B: Mid-Market / Recurring Services** | 25-40 accounts | $180M (36% of revenue) | 26% | $46.8M | $12M | +6.7% | Declining (28% → 26% in 2 yrs) | 8% | 38 (good) | **Medium**: Good retention, recurring revenue (maintenance contracts, predictable). **Profitability**: Marginally profitable; EBITDA trending down. **Issue**: Commoditized service line; pricing under pressure; scale not enough to justify premium model. |
| **Segment C: Project-Based / Custom Solutions** | 50-80 accounts | $85M (17% of revenue) | 18% | $15.3M | -$5M | -5.9% | Declining rapidly (24% → 18% in 2 yrs) | 15% | 28 (poor) | **Low**: Project churn, high volatility, poor NPS. Perpetually unprofitable. **Profitability**: Unprofitable; EBITDA negative. **Issue**: Custom work requires high-touch, non-scalable delivery; customer churn high; pricing discipline poor (bid wars, scope creep). **Verdict**: Structural unprofitability; should exit or radically reprrice. |
| **Segment D: Emerging / International** | 15-25 accounts | $30M (6% of revenue) | 15% | $4.5M | -$4M | -13% | Deteriorating (start 22% → 15% now) | 18% | 22 (poor) | **Very low**: New market, no scale, high cost-to-serve. Unprofitable, declining. **Issue**: Expansion strategy failed; cannot compete in emerging markets with current cost structure. **Verdict**: Exit or radically restructure. |
| **Segment E: Other / Long-Tail** | 200+ small | $30M (6% of revenue) | 12% | $3.6M | -$3M | -10% | Declining | 20% | <20 (very poor) | **None**: Low margin, high churn, unprofitable. Long tail of unprofitable small accounts consuming disproportionate overhead. |
| **TOTAL** | 300-350 | $495M | 25% | $123.75M | -$10M | -2% | - | 12% average | 31 average | - |

**Diagnostic Breakdown**:

1. **Profitable Segments (A + B = $380M, 77% of revenue)**:
   - **Segment A (Strategic)**: $200M, 12% EBITDA margin, stable. **Diagnosis**: This is the crown jewel. Profitable, sticky, but not growing. **Action**: Protect and grow selectively; leverage cross-divisional synergies.
   - **Segment B (Mid-Market Recurring)**: $180M, 6.7% EBITDA, declining. **Diagnosis**: Profitable but under margin pressure (commoditization). **Action**: Cost rationalization + selective price increases + differentiation initiatives could restore to 8-10% EBITDA.
   - **Combined Turnaround Potential**: If Segments A+B stabilized and grown 5-10%, could generate $24-30M EBITDA (vs. current loss of -$10M) = $34-40M swing.

2. **Unprofitable Segments (C + D + E = $145M, 29% of revenue)**:
   - **Segment C (Project-Based)**: $85M, -5.9% EBITDA. Structurally unprofitable. **Diagnosis**: High-touch, low-scale delivery model. Churn 15%, NPS 28. **Action**: Exit non-core projects; focus only on high-margin, recurring project types tied to Segment A; reduce to $30-40M revenue with 5%+ EBITDA, or divest entirely.
   - **Segment D + E (Emerging/Long-Tail)**: $60M, -$7M EBITDA. **Diagnosis**: Unprofitable ancillary businesses; consume overhead without generating return. **Action**: Exit entirely (cost structure doesn't support).
   - **Potential Exits**: Exiting C + D + E (reducing revenue from $495M to $350-380M) could cut EBITDA losses by $7M, and if done with cost structure reduction, could swing to break-even or small profit.

3. **Order Book Risk by Segment**:
   - **Segment A**: $480M order book (2.4x annual revenue) - healthy, sticky
   - **Segment B**: $280M order book (1.55x annual revenue) - at-risk, declining
   - **Segments C-E**: $90M order book (0.6x combined annual revenue) - critically low, imminent revenue cliff

**Diagnostic Conclusion from 1B**:
- **Salvageable core**: Segments A + B ($380M, profitable) can sustain viable business if margins stabilized and growth reignited. Profit potential = $25-30M EBITDA (5-8% margins).
- **Unredeemable tail**: Segments C + D + E ($145M, unprofitable) should be exited; eliminating them would increase consolidated EBITDA by $7M+ and improve returns on remaining business.
- **Customer concentration opportunity**: Top 8-12 Segment A customers = 40% of revenue, 60% of profit. Over-dependence on few customers is risk, but also implies: (a) if retained + grown, could drive significant EBITDA; (b) if lost, unit collapses.
- **Verdict**: Turnaround is feasible if focused on **Segments A + B**; exit is required if **Segment A erodes further or order book falls below $300M**.

#### Component 1C: Competitive Position & Win/Loss Analysis

**Objective**: Determine if losses are due to inferior competitive position (structural) or execution gaps (fixable).

| Assessment Area | Current Diagnostic Findings | Structural vs. Execution? | Strategic Implication |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Win/Loss Analysis (Last 20-30 Bids)** | Recent bidding summary: (1) **Losses to competitors**: Won 12/32 recent bids (37.5% win rate, vs. historical 45-50%). (2) **Primary loss reasons**: 60% lost on price (competitor 5-15% lower); 25% lost on perceived service quality / delivery risk; 15% lost on relationship / incumbent advantage. (3) **Price differential**: Average bid price = 8-12% above nearest competitor on comparable scope. Unit systematically priced 8-12 points higher. (4) **Service quality perception**: 65% of lost bids report "concerns about delivery timeline" or "uncertainty on project execution"; only 35% report quality concerns per se. | **EXECUTION**: Win-rate decline primarily price-driven, not quality-driven. Unit has higher cost structure (→ higher bid prices) than competitors, but **not demonstrably superior service**. This suggests: (a) cost structure misaligned with market expectations; (b) value proposition not clearly articulated / differentiated; (c) execution risk perceived as high (likely due to past project delays/overruns, visible to market). If cost structure can be reduced 10-15%, win rate could recover to 42-45%. **STRUCTURAL RISK**: If competitors have structural cost advantage (scale, vertical integration, labor arbitrage), unit cannot win on price without radical transformation. | **Turnaround lever**: Fix delivery execution (reduce schedule slippage, improve project margins) to restore confidence; rationalize cost to reduce bids 5-8%; focus sales on high-margin segments (Tier-1, recurring) where price less critical. **Exit trigger**: If delivery problems persist after 6 months of corrective action, or if 3-4 large strategic customers report dissatisfaction with execution. |
| **Competitive Benchmarking** | Peer comparison (vs. 3-4 similar mid-tier industrial-services competitors): (1) **Gross Margin**: Unit 25%, peers 28-32% (competitor advantage 300-700 bps). (2) **SG&A %**: Unit 23%, peers 18-20% (cost disadvantage 300-500 bps). (3) **EBITDA Margin**: Unit -2%, peers +8-12% (gap = 1,000+ bps). (4) **Utilization**: Unit 65%, peers 75-80%. (5) **Revenue per employee**: Unit $280K, peers $350-400K (labor productivity gap 20-25%). (6) **Customer satisfaction/NPS**: Unit 31, peers 40-50. | **MIXED**: Cost structure gap (SG&A 300-500 bps high) is fixable through operational efficiency. Margin gap partly due to cost structure, partly due to service-delivery issues (low utilization, project overruns, customer dissatisfaction). Not a scale problem (peers similar size); more of a **execution + operating model problem**. | **Turnaround lever**: (1) SG&A reduction plan: target 20% SG&A ratio (reduce $10-15M from $113.85M SG&A), close the cost gap to peers. (2) Utilization improvement: target 75% utilization (reduce field labor costs, improve project margins). (3) Customer satisfaction: launch quality/delivery improvement program; target NPS 40+ by Month 12. **Feasibility**: All three are execution improvements, not fundamental capability gaps. Likely achievable in 12 months. |
| **Service Line Profitability** | Breakdown by service type: (1) **Maintenance/Field Service** (recurring): $180M revenue, 28% margin, +5% EBITDA; growing slowly. **(2) Project Engineering/Design**: $140M revenue, 20% margin, +2% EBITDA; flat. (3) **Consulting/Advisory**: $85M revenue, 24% margin, +4% EBITDA; declining (customers prefer turnkey vs. time-and-materials). (4) **Emergency/24-7 Support**: $40M revenue, 22% margin, -3% EBITDA; unprofitable despite high perceived value. (5) **Custom Solutions / Specialized**: $50M revenue, 18% margin, -8% EBITDA; deeply unprofitable. | **EXECUTION**: (1) Maintenance/Field Service is profit engine; should be grown. (2) Project Engineering declining due to mix shift (customers increasingly want bundled, turnkey services, not just design). (3) Emergency/24-7 profitable in concept (high margin), but execution broken (over-provisioned, low utilization, customer responsiveness failures). (4) Custom Solutions perpetually unprofitable (high-touch, non-repeatable delivery). | **Turnaround levers**: (1) Focus on Maintenance/Field Service; expand from $180M with 5-8% EBITDA targets. (2) Restructure Project Engineering to be premium, project-management-led offering (not commoditized design); or exit. (3) Fix Emergency/24-7 execution; reduce cost base 20-30% while maintaining SLA compliance; could improve $40M line from -3% to +5% EBITDA ($3.2M swing). (4) Exit Custom Solutions entirely or narrow to strategic, high-margin projects only. **Feasibility**: Service-line restructuring is operational change, achievable in 9-12 months. |
| **Talent & Organization Retention** | (1) **Manager turnover**: Best 10-15 managers (P&L leads, senior technical) transferred out to other divisions or competitor in past 18 months. Visible to market (competitors recruiting internal talent = signal of trouble). (2) **Technical staff**: 20-25% attrition in field/technical roles (vs. 10% at peers). Low morale cited (uncertain future, flat comp vs. peers). (3) **Sales/BD**: Weak sales leadership; recent VP Sales departure; leads not being qualified / pursued aggressively. (4) **Org clarity**: Reorganizations (2 in 2 years) created confusion on decision rights, accountability blurred. | **EXECUTION**: Talent exodus is symptom, not cause. Root cause = uncertainty (losses, restructuring rumors, unclear strategy). Losing good people accelerates business decline (lower quality delivery, weaker sales effort). **Feedback loop**: Losses → uncertainty → turnover → lower quality → more losses. However, **positive:** Talent available; if company commits to turnaround + clearly signals stability, can re-attract or rebuild. | **Turnaround lever**: Clear communication of turnaround plan (Month 1-2); retention bonuses for key people ($200-500K total); performance-based upside (EBITDA recovery targets met → bonuses triggered). **Dependency**: Must stabilize org first; without clarity, talent exodus will accelerate, making turnaround impossible by Month 12. **Exit signal**: If top 10 leaders signal departure intentions by Month 4, turnaround becomes unachievable (execution risk too high). |

**Diagnostic Conclusion from 1C**:
- **Competitive position recoverable**: Unit is not fundamentally inferior (not like "we build product at 2x cost of competitors"). Rather, cost structure and execution are misaligned with market expectations. Fixable through operational discipline.
- **Key execution gaps**: Cost structure (SG&A 300-500 bps above peers); utilization (65% vs. 75%+ peers); delivery reliability (NPS 31 vs. 40+ peers); organization stability (turnover high).
- **Win rate recoverable**: If cost structure reduced 8-12% AND delivery execution improved, win rate should recover from 37.5% to 42-45% within 9-12 months.
- **Verdict**: Losses appear **60% execution-driven, 40% structural**. Turnaround feasible if addressed rapidly and decisively.

### 1.2 Cash Flow & Working Capital Diagnostic

**Objective**: Understand if cash burn is accelerating (unsustainable) or stable (can survive 12-month turnaround window).

| Cash Flow Component | Year -2 | Year -1 | Year 0 | Trend | Diagnostic Implication |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Operating Cash Flow** | $12M | -$8M | -$18M | Deteriorating rapidly | **CRITICAL**: Unit burning cash and accelerating. At current burn rate ($18M/year), runway is 12-18 months. **Implication**: Turnaround must show positive cash flow by Month 9 or liquidity crisis emerges. |
| **Working Capital Change (Cash Outflow)** | -$5M | -$6.9M | -$9M | Deteriorating | Working capital tied up $9M additional capital in Year 0 (inventory build, receivables stretched). If trend continues, will consume additional $9-10M cash in Year 1. **Action**: Must stabilize working capital immediately (inventory reduction, receivables collection, payables timing). |
| **Capex** | $8M | $6M | $4M | Declining | Unit under-investing in equipment/tools (cost-cutting response). **Risk**: Aging equipment may impact service delivery quality / project timeliness. **Opportunity**: Capex can be deferred to zero or minimal in Year 1 turnaround phase (focus on operational improvement, not capital expansion). |
| **Free Cash Flow** | -$1M | -$14.9M | -$22M | Deeply negative, accelerating | At current trajectory, unit will run out of cash without parent support within 12-18 months. **Strategic implication**: Board patience is real (one-year deadline), but cash-flow timeline is even tighter. Turnaround must show positive FCF by Month 9-10. |
| **Days Sales Outstanding (DSO)** | 42 days | 46 days | 52 days | Increasing (collection deterioration) | Customers paying slower (52-day average = extended terms given to win business, or collection problems). **Cash impact**: If collected in 45 days instead of 52, would free up $4-5M working capital (52-42 days = 10 days × $500M revenue / 365). **Opportunity**: Collection improvement = quick cash win (no operational change needed). |
| **Inventory Turnover** | 8x annually | 7.2x annually | 6.5x annually | Declining (inventory bloat) | Inventory growing faster than revenue (obsolete stock, poor inventory management). **Cash impact**: If turnover recovered to 8x, would reduce inventory by $5-7M. **Action**: Inventory reduction audit; write-off obsolete stock. |
| **Days Payable Outstanding (DPO)** | 35 days | 35 days | 35 days | Stable | Paying suppliers on 35-day cycle. Opportunity: If extended to 45 days (industry standard), would generate $5-7M working capital relief. **Risk**: Must not damage supplier relationships (particularly critical suppliers). **Approach**: Negotiate extended terms with non-critical suppliers; offer early-payment discount for strategic suppliers. |

**Diagnostic Conclusion from 1.2**:
- **Cash burn is unsustainable**: $22M free cash flow burn in Year 0; at this rate, unit is insolvent within 12-18 months without parent funding.
- **But turnaround can address**: Working capital improvements (inventory + receivables + payables) could generate $12-15M cash within 6 months (quick wins). Combined with EBITDA stabilization (Month 6-9), can achieve cash-flow break-even by Month 9-10.
- **Window is tight**: Turnaround must show clear cash-flow path within Months 1-3 diagnostic or board will force exit earlier.

## PART 2: TARGETED TURNAROUND PLAN (MONTHS 4-12)

### 2.1 Profit Recovery Roadmap by Segment

**Objective**: Design specific, measurable initiatives to restore profitability to target levels ($12-18M EBITDA by Month 12).

#### Segment A: Tier-1 Strategic / Cross-Divisional ($200M, current +12% EBITDA = +$24M)

| Initiative | Baseline (Month 0) | Target (Month 12) | Mechanism | Investment Required | Owner | Milestone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Revenue Growth (Protect & Grow)** | $200M | $215M (+7.5% growth) | (1) Cross-divisional bundling: identify 5-8 Tier-1 customers buying from multiple divisions; bundle services → volume increase + stickiness. Target: 2-3 customers add $5-10M incremental services. (2) Upsell retention: 12 Tier-1 customers at risk of reduction; protective visits + value-add proposals → retain 90% of current volume. (3) New logos: 2-3 new strategic accounts in target sectors; requires 6-month sales cycle; launch Month 2. | $500K (sales team augmentation, bundling study) | VP Sales + Cross-Div Exec Sponsor | Month 6: Cross-div bundling plan finalized; Month 9: +$5M pipeline identified; Month 12: achieve $215M (or $208M+ floor) |
| **Margin Protection & Expansion** | 32% | 33-34% (+100-200 bps) | (1) Price realization: current 32% margin includes 2-3% annual price increases committed pre-contract. Negotiate renewal price increases 3-5% for 50% of customer base (tied to value-add, CPI pass-through). Target: capture +1.5-2.5% pricing uplift. (2) Cost optimization: selective process efficiency improvements (documentation, scheduling) → labor cost reduction 2-3%; combined with price increases = 100-200 bps margin expansion. (3) Avoid mix degradation: ensure no migration to lower-margin service lines; protect highest-margin activities. | $300K (pricing strategy, analytics) | CFO + P&L Lead | Month 4: Pricing plan by customer; Month 8: 50% of price increases negotiated; Month 12: realize 33-34% margin |
| **Order Book Stabilization** | $480M (2.4x revenue) | $500M+ (2.3x revenue) | (1) Contract renewals: ensure all 12 Tier-1 contracts extending into Year 2 are renewed by Month 9. Proactive renewal negotiations Month 4-6. (2) Expansion contracts: bundle initiatives (above) should add $10-15M to pipeline; formalize as proposals Month 7-8. (3) Win rate improvement: if Tier-1 bids improving (cost structure fixed), win rate on new Tier-1 opportunities should improve from 37% to 45%+. Target: 3-4 new wins ($15-20M) in Year 1. | Included in sales investment above | VP Sales | Month 6: 90% of critical renewals secured; Month 9: $15-20M new opportunities formalized; Month 12: Order book $500M+ |
| **Execution Excellence & NPS** | NPS 45 (strong baseline) | NPS 48-50 (top-quartile) | (1) Delivery consistency: zero late deliveries; proactive client communication; document SLA compliance. (2) Client satisfaction initiatives: quarterly business reviews; executive sponsorship model (Div President → Tier-1 customer); annual customer council. (3) Capture feedback: post-project reviews; identify service improvement opportunities. | $200K (client satisfaction programs) | COO + Client Success Lead | Monthly NPS tracking; Month 6: NPS 47; Month 12: NPS 48-50 |
| **TOTAL IMPACT (Segment A)** | +$24M EBITDA ($200M × 12%) | +$29M EBITDA ($215M × 13.5%) | **EBITDA upside**: +$5M vs. baseline | $1M | VP Sales + COO | **Month 12 target: Defend $24M + grow to $29M** |

**Rationale for Segment A Focus**:
- **Profitable, growing segment**: Least risky; highest-probability wins. If protected + grown 7.5%, generates additional $5M EBITDA.
- **Cross-divisional leverage**: Strategic customers often buy from multiple divisions; bundling creates competitive advantage vs. pure industrial-services competitors.
- **Sticky, long-term relationships**: Low churn (3%), NPS already strong (45); investment in deepening relationships has high ROI.
- **Win rate less price-sensitive**: Tier-1 customers value reliability + quality over low price; improving execution → improving win rate + margins.

---

#### Segment B: Mid-Market / Recurring Services ($180M, current +6.7% EBITDA = +$12M)

| Initiative | Baseline (Month 0) | Target (Month 12) | Mechanism | Investment Required | Owner | Milestone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Revenue Stabilization & Growth** | $180M | $190M (+5.6% growth) | (1) Churn reduction: 8% annual churn = $14.4M revenue loss; if reduce to 6%, saves $3.6M. Mechanism: retention campaigns targeting at-risk accounts; value-add proposals (efficiency improvements, service enhancements); price justification. (2) Same-account growth: penetration of 15-20 high-potential accounts; upsell additional service lines; target: +$4-6M from account expansion. (3) New logos: add 5-8 new SMB accounts in recurring maintenance category; requires active lead gen. Target: +$3-4M new revenue. **Net impact**: Reduce churn + expansion + new logos = +$10M (vs. baseline -$3.6M churn = $13.6M swing). | $400K (customer retention, lead gen, sales) | VP Sales + Segment P&L Lead | Month 6: Retention plan by account; Month 9: +$5M expansion pipeline; Month 12: achieve $190M |
| **Margin Recovery (Target: 28% from 26%)** | 26% ($46.8M GP) | 28% ($53.2M GP) | (1) **Price optimization**: Recurring contracts often have annual CPI adjustments; enforce full 3-4% CPI pass-through (often foregone). Target: +1.5-2% uplift. (2) **Cost rationalization**: (a) Standardize service delivery model → reduce per-call labor cost 5-10%. (b) Route optimization (AI-based dispatch) → reduce travel time 10-15%. (c) Maintenance intervals optimization (predictive maintenance) → reduce reactive emergency calls 15-20%, improve margin mix. **Combined**: 2-3% cost reduction = 200 bps margin improvement. (3) **Mix shift**: Move customer base toward higher-margin maintenance vs. lower-margin emergency support. Target: 65% recurring, 35% reactive (vs. current 60/40). | $800K (cost rationalization: dispatch system, predictive maintenance pilots, process redesign) | COO + Finance | Month 5: Pricing review by customer; Month 8: 50% of cost initiatives deployed; Month 12: achieve 28% margin |
| **Customer
